Source: Finnegan, R., Moore, J.R., and Geimer, P.R. (2021), Data for
"Vibration of Natural Rock Arches and Towers Excited by Helicopter-Sourced Infrasound".
University of Utah Research Data Repository (The Hive).
https://doi.org/10.7278/S50D-41SW-THMA
https://hive.utah.edu/records/vz3dr-1n993

License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported.

This fixture preserves all exported measured ridges from all three complete
140-minute TwoBridge pressure-microphone channels, with ordinary production
discovery at main 5dcb54f. Conversion retained every sample at the native 200 Hz,
using the published 8.744e-5 Pa/count factor, one common linear power-of-two gain
and float32 quantization. No filtering, resampling, cropping, signals, trajectories
or recording clocks were generated. GPX positions were not discovery inputs.

All six original groups and their failures are retained. The existing full-group
joint model accepted two and rejected four; those results are software/model
controls, not independently verified aircraft identity, clock, location or
detection-accuracy evidence. These simultaneous channels are not independent
field sessions or a sealed holdout. Microphone survey and clock uncertainty
remain unproven. No private data or data-owner outreach was used.
